name: A — Won't stop 'til it's over
concept: One long golden memory: letterboxed and hushed through the verses, the frame snaps open to full screen on the climax.
references: Super 8 home movies, Call Me by Your Name, The Temper Trap's own sun-bleached video
look: golden grade + faded, light leaks on downbeats, 2.39 letterbox that opens at 'won't stop'
type: tiny Playfair italic: one sung word per photo ('a moment', 'a love', ...)
motion: slow pushes, dissolves, double exposures of faces over skies; one hard cut at the climax
signature: the litany ('a moment, a love, a dream, aloud...') one photo per sung word, then the letterbox bursting open on 'won't stop 'til it's over'

name: B — A kiss, a cry
concept: Black-and-white editorial: every word of the litany becomes a giant window onto a different photo; the chorus stacks in huge type.
references: Swiss poster typography, Saul Bass title sequences, Apple's black-and-white typographic ads
look: punchy black & white, one red accent
type: Anton knockouts and stacked kinetic lyrics on the sung syllables; mono index numbers (04 / 08)
motion: hard cuts on downbeats, slices on the drums, a zoom-through the last word into colour
signature: 'won't stop 'til it's over' builds word by word, then the camera dives through the O into the only colour shot of the film

name: C — Blood's still young
concept: A risograph tour zine of the summer: torn two-ink collages pile up on the beat, and the climax turns into a riso kaleidoscope.
references: DIY punk zines, risograph print studios, 90s skate-video editing
look: riso in fluoro pink + blue (green at the drop), xerox for contrast, misregistration
type: Anton stamps, page numbers ('No. 6'), ransom-note place names
motion: collage builds per 8th, filmstrip scrolls, kaleido + strobe at the climax
signature: the drop: the whole frame folds into a kaleidoscope of the group hug with 'WON'T STOP' stamped in the centre
